newsitem.title: INDIA: India regional group plans to quit coalition.
newsitem.headline: India regional group plans to quit coalition.

text.p: India's regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party said on Monday it was planning to to pull out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's centre-left United Front coalition.

The party, to which Industry Minister Murasoli Maran belongs, said in a statement it planned to continue support from outside for Gujral's government, but cited differences over the conduct of some unnamed coalition partners.
DMK leaders blamed the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), accusing it of interfering in Gujral's Janata Dal party.
There was no immediate threat to Gujral's government.
The DMK accounts less than a tenth the United Front's 178 seats in the 545-member lower house of parliament, and depends on make-or-break support from the Congress party, which has 140 members.

"The DMK is not willing to go along with the personal whims of some leaders and the private minimum programmes of certain parties," the regional party's president, Muthuvel Karunanidhi, said in a statement in Madras, capital of the state of Tamil Nadu.
"Until the situation improves, the DMK is planning to stay out of the ministry and support the government from outside," Karunanidhi, who is also the state's chief minister said in the statement.

The statement did not give details, but party politicians said it was directed at the CPI-M, which has taken a hardline against a petroleum price hike and against admitting a breakaway political group of Gujral's Janata Dal party.

"We are angry with the communists who are unnecessarily creating complications," a state government minister told Reuters. "We believe the CPM is interfering too much in the affairs of the Janata Dal."
But DMK leaders said they had no differences with the CPI-M's objections to proposals to hike oil prices and cut fuel subsidies.

They said the main point of difference was over attempts to force out of the coalition in the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), formed earlier this month by Laloo Prasad Yadav, who was earlier president of the Janata Dal.
Yadav formed his breakaway RJD on July 5, citing alleged malpractices in party elections held two days before that.

Yadav has refused calls led by the CPI-M to resign as chief minister of his eastern state of Bihar after being indicted by the federal police in a $280-million corruption scandal involving the alleged diversion of animal welfare funds.
Yadav says he is innocent of the charges.

The CPI-M wants his group to be kept out of Gujral's coalition unless he resigns to face trial. Gujral has been hinting that Yadav should resign but has not agreed to sack three of his loyalists from the federal ministry.
